title: A reusable document pipeline
summary: Technical decisions behind a structured PRD, a standalone reader and focused context for each task.
constraints: Reading a document requires no hosted service.
No automatic commits, pushes or publication.
Planned checks are never presented as observed results.

entries.title: One source, multiple views
entries.body: Specifications are currently written in Markdown and converted to HTML. Dependencies and traceability tables are maintained separately. The new engine produces these views from structured data.

entries.title: Separate content from presentation
entries.body: The model writes requirements, decisions and tasks in versioned JSON. The engine owns the structure, components and rendering rules. The HTML document embeds its data and works offline.
entries.alternative: Keep Markdown and only improve the stylesheet. This option makes little difference to focused extraction and reference validation.
entries.consequences: The schema must remain flexible enough for business explanations. A new schema version requires an explicit migration.

entries.title: Approved content remains identifiable
entries.body: Gate B approves the technical plan and execution tasks together. SHA-256 digests of both JSON sources bind evidence to that exact combined plan. Editing either source makes the previous execution record stale even if its revision number has not changed.

entries.title: Data is never executed as instructions
entries.body: Content is displayed as text. Seed and validation commands are instructions to inspect, never scripts executed by the reader. Internal links use validated identifiers.

entries.title: From JSON to a readable document
entries.body: Validation resolves task references against the technical plan before rendering one approval document. The reader shows technical logic, then tasks and checks. Each agent receives only its owned task and relevant contracts.
entries.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Author
  participant Validator
  participant Reader
  participant Agent
  Author->>Validator: Technical plan and execution tasks
  Validator->>Validator: Validate IDs, references and dependency graph
  Validator->>Reader: Combined plan with diagrams
  Reader-->>Author: Gate B review
  Author->>Agent: Approved task context
  Agent-->>Reader: Separate execution evidence

entries.title: Calculate ready tasks
entries.body: After Gates A and B, a task can start once its dependencies have validated implementations and its write scope does not overlap an active task. Independent tasks can run together. Review and corrections run on the integrated result after all code tasks validate; each task then retains its own local checkpoint or small PR/MR. Acceptance tasks remain assigned to a person.
entries.example: CODE-001 and CODE-005 can start together. Once CODE-001 validates, CODE-002 and CODE-003 can run concurrently because their write scopes are disjoint. They do not wait for CODE-001 to be published.

entries.title: Prepare pull requests without publishing
entries.body: The helper captures the diff and its exact base. The model explains the change from this snapshot. A final check detects a changed branch or included planning documents before authorized publication.

entries.title: Install a verified version
entries.body: Test the engine and scripts in a local copy. Keep a backup of previous files and verify they have not changed before replacing them. Existing HTML documents remain readable.
